messages:
mike: FYI PR #8401 (scheduler/tiling) canary shows a p95 uptick on 4k seq. can we get quick eyes? bench: https://bench.redwood.internal/run/xyz

alice: looking now. which canary id?

mike: shard-pack-tiling-v3, canary id c-2026-03-17-18, us-west-2 cluster.

jen: I pulled artifacts — p95 looks ~52ms -> ~98ms, p99 ~90 -> ~182. throughput same. jotting the numbers below.

sam: short summary plz, is memory changing?

jen: short paste:
```
model: llama-2-7b
batch: 8
seq_len: 4096
p50: 18ms -> 20ms
p95: 52ms -> 98ms
p99: 90ms -> 182ms
memory: 13.4GB -> 14.1GB
```

sam: ok mem +700MB, that could amplify tail. any obvious contention in trace?

mike: uploaded hotspots trace: https://artifacts.redwood/trace/abc123 (stack sampled around allocate()/prefetch_manager)

alexa: quick read: the PR introduced a global prefetch_manager.lock around allocate(). that serializes per-request prefetch. probable cause for the tail.

mike: yep the diff is small but unfortunate. code snippet in PR:
```diff
- prefetch_manager.lock()
- allocate(shard)
- prefetch_manager.unlock()
+ allocate_with_prefetch(shard)
```

alexa: I can propose a narrower scope: per-shard lock instead of global. will push patch in a few mins.

ci-bot: canary status: degraded — p95 increased by 88% (auto-signal).

jen: unless alexa's hotfix lands quickly, hold merge please. this should block the merge queue.

mike: filing a hold now (PR label: hold/merge) and pinging reviewers.

karen: tagging SRE in case we need a revert: @oncall-sre can standby for revert if canary worsens.

alexa: pushed a micro-fix (moves lock to per-shard map). bench artifacts attached to PR. small smoke locally looks like p95 back to ~54ms.

mike: running a quick canary re-run now. will drop results when done. thx all :thumbsup:

jen: thanks — if re-run clean, remove hold and request merge window. if not, we'll revert.

mike: re-run finished: p95 56ms, p99 95ms, mem 13.5GB. patch looks good. removing hold and requesting merge slot in next window.

alexa: cool, will add a short note in PR explaining root cause and the lock-scope change.

mike: filing follow-up ticket to add a unit test for prefetch concurrency to avoid regression. https://tickets.redwood/INC-5123
